notes: OUTCOME: src/best.js adds readBest(storage) and writeBest(storage, wave), and both take the storage object as an argument. readBest returns the saved wave as a number, and null when the value is missing, not a number or not a whole wave. writeBest only ever raises the best, writes over an unreadable value (the test with 'seven' then 3 shows this), and leaves a real best alone when handed an invalid wave.

OUTCOME: src/main.js saves the wave through bestAfterStep. It writes only on the frame where the status moves from 'playing' to 'won' or 'lost', so each run is saved once, before any restart click. The test that plays a real game to a loss records exactly one write across five more frames. The best is read at boot and passed to draw. Using browserStorage() instead of the bare localStorage global is sound: reading localStorage throws a SecurityError when the browser has storage turned off, and this keeps the game running in that case.

OUTCOME: src/render.js draws 'Best: wave N' on the existing start screen only when best is not null, between the tagline and the Start button. test/best.test.js uses a recording context to check that the drawn text includes 'Best: wave 7' and that no Best text appears when there is no best. The new best parameter defaults to null, so existing callers of draw are unaffected.

CONSTRUCTION: no defect found. A storage that is missing or throws reads as no best, and a refused write is swallowed. An invalid wave (0, a fraction, NaN, undefined, or the string '9') is never saved. A playing game draws the same text whether or not a best is passed.
